records.name: Sawubona Creativity Project
records.summary: A South Philadelphia theatre group that teaches improv, acting and storytelling to adults, kids and teens. It also runs free Sunday improv jams, summer camps and family shows at its theatre space.
records.what_you_do: Take an adult improv or acting class, sign a child or teen up for a theatre class or camp, join a free Sunday jam, or come to a family show.

schedule.text: Free improv jams and workshops are held every Sunday. Adult and kids classes and a summer camp are offered too, and the website lists current dates and times.

cost.text: Class fees are listed on the website but were not on the pages we could read. The Sunday jams are free, and a fiscal sponsor's page says some workshops and family shows are free too.

first_step.how: Come to a free Sunday improv jam, or try the free workshop on the group's flyer (it links through a QR code), then sign up for a class on the website.
first_step.basis: Classes and the free jams are open to the public and there is a free trial, but the pages do not say beginners are welcome or who can attend the Queer and BIPOC jams.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe a jam or a class in detail, so ask how long one lasts before you go. Classes only run if enough students sign up, and refunds are not given, but you can move to another class that has not started if you email the studio first.
first_visit_tips: Email or call before a first class to ask about the level and how long it runs, since the site does not say.
Read the class policy first: there are no refunds, and a class can be cancelled if too few people enroll.
The page does not say who the Queer and BIPOC improv jams are for, so ask before you go.
The entrance and parking are not described, so call 856-332-4951 for directions.

records.notes: Tier 1 had Sunday evening from a single event listing. Sunday is kept for the free weekly jams, but the evening time was removed because no page read gives a time. Summer camp 2026 runs themed weeks from late June to mid August; one title appears twice with different dates, so confirm camp dates before signing up. The upcoming shows page lists no dates. The Improv and Acting Classes menu link points to the homepage, so no separate class detail was found. Fractured Atlas is the project's fiscal sponsor, not a joinable group, so it was not listed as a lead. Status and last_sign_of_life are kept from tier 1 (creativephl event).

records.name: School District of Philadelphia classroom volunteers
records.summary: Lets a Philadelphia resident volunteer in a public school classroom once the school agrees and the volunteer has finished the required clearances and orientation.
records.what_you_do: Help a teacher in a classroom at a school you choose. Before you start, you complete the required checks, the district's volunteer orientation, and a code of conduct signed for the principal.

schedule.text: How often you come is set with the school. The district page does not give a schedule or a time commitment.

locations.label: A Philadelphia public school, arranged with the school first

cost.text: No program fee. The state child abuse history and criminal history checks are free. An FBI fingerprint check costs $23.25, and applies only if you have not lived in Pennsylvania for the past 10 years.

first_step.how: Ask the school whether it needs volunteers, then start the free clearances and sign up for the district's volunteer orientation.
first_step.basis: Volunteers must finish clearances, an orientation and a principal's sign-off before they start, so you see the classroom only after the paperwork.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most of the first stretch is paperwork: the child abuse history clearance, the state criminal history check, and either an FBI check with fingerprints or a signed affirmation if you have lived in Pennsylvania for 10 years. Next comes the orientation, either an online webinar of about 45 minutes with a short quiz or an in person session led by a family engagement liaison. The page does not say how often volunteers come or how long they stay.
first_visit_tips: Check with the school first, because each school decides whether it needs volunteers.
Start the child abuse history clearance early, since the page says results can take up to 14 days.
Finish the orientation within 45 days of starting, and hand the signed code of conduct to the principal.
If you have not lived in Pennsylvania for the past 10 years, pre-enroll with IdentoGo before your fingerprint appointment.

records.notes: The volunteer checklist is a Google Drive document that was not opened, so it may list further forms. Phone 215-400-4180 is the district office line (440 N. Broad St., Suite 114), not a volunteer-only line. The deep read found no date on the page itself, so the tier 1 status and date were kept; a reviewer may prefer probably_active.

records.name: Schuylkill Banks
records.summary: The group that cares for the southern eight miles of the Schuylkill River trail, from Fairmount Dam to the Delaware River. It runs public events on the trail and the water, and volunteers help keep the trail clean and green and help run those events.
records.what_you_do: Volunteer on trail care, such as picking up litter, pulling invasive plants, planting and spreading mulch, or help with events like kayak tours and movie nights. You can also come to a public event.

schedule.text: Trail work runs weekdays 10 am to 4 pm and weekends 10 am to 1 pm, in sessions of at least three hours. Help with events happens on select Thursdays, Saturdays and Sundays in warmer months.

locations.label: Schuylkill River Trail, Fairmount Dam to the Delaware River

cost.text: Events are described as a mix of free and low-cost activities. Prices are not listed on the pages we could read.

first_step.how: Fill in the volunteer form on the website with your name, email and interests. For a different day or a group visit, contact the group first.
first_step.basis: Anyone can send in the public volunteer form, but the page does not mention a first-time orientation or training.
first_step.what_to_expect: Trail sessions last at least three hours and usually run 10 am to 4 pm on weekdays or 10 am to 1 pm on weekends. The work can include picking up litter, removing graffiti, pulling invasive plants, planting, and spreading mulch or gravel. Event help covers setup, checking people in, carrying kayaks to and from the water, handing out refreshments and cleanup.
first_visit_tips: Plan for at least three hours, and check the weekday or weekend hours before you go.
Groups of up to 12 can volunteer together, so contact the group first to set up a group day.
If you need a different day, ask, since the page says scheduling can be flexible.
The email address sits behind a protected link, so use the contact page or call 215-309-5523.

records.notes: The volunteer page names Schuylkill River Development Corporation as the operator, with its office at 2401 Walnut Street, Suite 603, Philadelphia, PA 19103. The events page lists movie nights, riverboat and kayak tours, and community celebrations, but shows no dates. The kayak tours, movie nights and community events pages returned 404, so those details are not confirmed. No dated item was found, so status stays probably_active and no last_sign_of_life is recorded.

records.name: Scribe Video Center
records.summary: A Philadelphia media arts center that teaches video, sound, film and digital media workshops, rents production gear to people who can show they know how to use it, and runs community video projects. Members get discounts on programs and equipment rental.
records.what_you_do: Take a video or digital media workshop, rent production gear once you show you can use it, or go to the free orientation for new members. You can also join the volunteer list for screenings and events.

schedule.text: The office is open Monday to Friday 10 am to 6 pm, with some weeknight and Saturday workshops. Workshops meet for one or more sessions, from one day to several weeks, and the FAQ suggests calling ahead.

cost.text: Workshops are paid. Listed prices run about $30 to $150 for non-members, with lower member prices. The new member orientation is free. A basic membership is $35 a year and gives a discount on programs.

first_step.how: Go to the free Orientation to Scribe for new members (the next ones are listed for Nov 9, 2026 and Jan 11, 2027), or register for an intro workshop such as Introduction to Adobe Premiere.
first_step.basis: The center has a free orientation for new members, labels several workshops as introductory or suited to first-time filmmakers, and says how to register on its site.
first_step.what_to_expect: Most workshops meet in person at the Lancaster Avenue center for one or more sessions, usually a few hours each. You can register online, by mail, in person or by phone with a credit card. Equipment rental is a separate step: you must show you can use the gear and get approval from the facilities manager.
first_visit_tips: Call ahead before you visit. The office keeps weekday hours and runs extra nights and Saturdays only when workshops are on.
Payments are usually not refunded, but you can change your registration up to 5 days before a workshop starts at no charge. Check dates first.
The directions list the Route 10 or T1 trolley and the Route 43 bus. No stop is named, so check a transit app before you go.
Take a workshop before you rent gear, since rental needs a skills check and approval.

records.notes: The membership pages at scribe.org/membership and scribe.org/join returned 404; the working page is scribe.org/join-us, which lists six yearly levels from $35 (Basic). The FAQ text shows a 2015 submission date, so its general details (hours, rental rule) may be old; the workshop listing and join page are current. Listings run from October 2026 to February 2027, so the tier 1 season (fall) was dropped. No page read covers accessibility or parking.

records.name: SEAMAAC Growing Home Gardens
records.summary: Two community gardens on Emily and Mercy Streets in South Philadelphia, run by SEAMAAC, an immigrant and refugee services nonprofit, with the Neighborhood Gardens Trust. Mostly immigrant and refugee gardeners grow vegetables and familiar foods here. We could not confirm current activity.
records.what_you_do: Rent an individual plot in one of the two food gardens and grow vegetables and familiar foods. Ask the gardens office about open plots and any yearly fee before you visit.

schedule.text: Plots are worked through the growing season. No meeting or work-day schedule is published.

first_step.how: Email gardens@seamaac.org or call (347) 719-1488 to ask about open plots and the yearly fee.
first_step.basis: The gardens are meant for newly arrived immigrants and refugees, and a contact is listed, but the pages do not say how to get a plot or whether there is a waitlist.
first_step.what_to_expect: The pages we read do not describe a first visit, how plots are given out, or when work days happen. The Neighborhood Gardens Trust page says the plots are individual, so you would grow on your own plot. Ask the gardens office what the first steps are when you call.
first_visit_tips: Call or email first, since the pages do not describe a walk-in visit.
Ask about open plots, the yearly fee and any waitlist before you go.
Ask which languages the gardens office speaks, since the site does not list languages.

records.notes: Newest dated evidence on the group's pages is an October 15, 2020 blog post that names SEAMAAC and the Emily Street gardens. The blog says 800 block of Emily Street, while the city and NGT lists give 728 to 42 Emily St (700 block); the record uses the list address. The SEAMAAC community page has an undated COVID-era update (footer 2021, photos from 2020). The SEAMAAC homepage has no dated news and does not mention the gardens. The NGT page does not say whether the gardens are active. Tier 1 had last_sign_of_life 2026-10 from the city friends list. The ArcGIS layer metadata shows a last edit of 2026-08-07 for the whole list, and the part we could read has no row for this garden, so it is not evidence the garden is active. Status is set to dormant under the 24-month rule. The reviewer should confirm with gardens@seamaac.org or set the status to unknown. The Neighborhood Gardens Trust is listed in leads_only. The Pennsylvania Horticultural Society is also named as a partner and is not listed separately.

records.name: Second State Press
records.summary: A nonprofit printmaking studio in Philadelphia that teaches hand printing methods, from stone lithography to screen printing, and lets artist members rent studio time. It also holds exhibitions and Second Thursday events.
records.what_you_do: Take an intro or beginner printmaking class, become an artist member and use the studio, or come to the exhibitions and Second Thursday events.

schedule.text: The studio is open Wednesday to Friday 12 to 8 pm and Saturday and Sunday 10 am to 6 pm, and is closed Monday and Tuesday. Classes are posted as dated listings, and the studio also holds Second Thursday events and exhibitions.

cost.text: Each class has its own price, which the class list does not show. Artist membership is $50 a year and is needed for studio access, and a Supporter membership is $100 a year.

first_step.how: Register for an intro class from the printmaking classes page, such as Intro to Riso Printing (listed for Oct 11, 2026).
first_step.basis: Many classes are tagged beginner-friendly or labeled intro, and each class has its own page with a link to sign up.
first_step.what_to_expect: Intro classes are short, usually a single session of about 2.5 to 5 hours, and teach the basics of one method such as riso, screen printing, lino or letterpress. The class list does not show prices, so check each class page before you sign up. The studio is in the Crane Arts Building, and the site gives no parking or transit details.
first_visit_tips: Riso printing on your own needs an Intro to Riso class or relevant riso experience, so take that class first.
The studio is self-guided and members are expected to know their own process, so an intro class helps before you rent studio time alone.
Several earlier listings are marked sold out, so check the class page for open spots before you travel.
Parking and transit are not on the site, so check directions to the Crane Arts Building before you go.

records.notes: The membership page at www.secondstatepress.org/membership returned 404; the working page is secondstatepress.org/about-membership. A Studio FAQs page is linked from the facilities page and was not fetched. The site writes the address as 1400 American St. without North; the tier 1 address with North is kept. The footer shows a 2025 copyright, which is not used as evidence. No page read covers accessibility or parking.

records.name: Senior Companion Program (Philadelphia Corporation for Aging)
records.summary: Volunteers aged 55 and up who visit older adults living at home who are lonely, isolated or have health or sight challenges, offering friendship, steady company and some practical help.
records.what_you_do: Visit one older adult at home on a regular schedule, keep them company, and help with small tasks such as sorting mail, light meals or getting to medical appointments. You complete a background check and paid training first.

schedule.text: Volunteers need to be able to serve about 20 hours a week, visiting one older adult on a regular schedule.

locations.label: PCA main office (visits happen where the older adult lives)

cost.text: No cost to volunteer. Volunteers receive a tax-free hourly stipend, travel and meal reimbursement, and paid holiday, sick and vacation time, and their training is paid.

first_step.how: Fill in the online volunteer application, then call 215-765-9000 ext. 5124 or email seniorcp@pcacares.org with questions about the next steps.
first_step.basis: You apply, meet an income guideline and pass a criminal background check before service, and the site does not say what a first visit looks like.
first_step.what_to_expect: The site does not describe the first visit. Before you serve, you complete a criminal background check and paid pre-service training, though the site does not say which comes first. After that you get four hours of ongoing training each month while you serve about 20 hours a week.
first_visit_tips: Check that you can give about 20 hours a week before you apply, because the application asks about it.
Be ready to say how you get around: the application asks about your own car, SEPTA or CCT Connect.
Ask when the background check and paid training start, since the site does not say which comes first.

records.notes: Two numbers appear on the group's own site. The program page says to call 215-422-4888 to learn more, while the application page gives 215-765-9000 ext. 5124 and seniorcp@pcacares.org. The record uses the application page contact, so confirm which line is current. The PCA Helpline (215-765-9040) is for general volunteer questions. The stipend amount is not published, and the order of background check and training is not stated. The SeniorCenters page does not describe this program. AmeriCorps Seniors is named as federal support and was not researched as a separate record. The tier 1 WHYY article (2025-07) was not re-read in this pass.
